Hasbaya.fact: The tower in the southwest corner and the eastern wall-both visible from the third floor – are easily identifiable as Crusader. Wide steps lead to the main entrance, where the original Crusader door still swings smoothly on 800-year-old hinges.

Hasbaya.question: Wide steps lead to the main entrance, where the original _____ door still swings smoothly on 800-year-old hinges
Hasbaya.fact: The tower in the southwest corner and the eastern wall-both visible from the third floor – are easily identifiable as Crusader. Wide steps lead to the main entrance, where the original Crusader door still swings smoothly on 800-year-old hinges.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: Stone lions, a heraldic emblem of the _____ family, decorate the wall on either side of the arched portal
Hasbaya.fact: Stone lions, a heraldic emblem of the Chehab family, decorate the wall on either side of the arched portal. A set of smaller lions appears within the arch above the doorway and just below that is a plaque in Arabic commemorating an addition to the castle made in the year 1009 Hejira by Emir Ali Chehab some 400 years ago.

Hasbaya.fact: 10.63% of the voters were Sunni Muslims.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations

Hasbaya.fact: Owned by the Chehab emirs, the citadel forms the major part of a Chehabi compound – a group of buildings surrounding an unpaved central square 150 metres long and 100 metres wide.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: Won by the _____ from the Crusaders in 1172, the fortress was rebuilt by its new owners
Hasbaya.fact: Won by the Chehabs from the Crusaders in 1172, the fortress was rebuilt by its new owners. Amazingly, for almost all of the eight centuries since it fell to the Chehabs, the citadel has been occupied by members of the same family.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: The upper floor has _____ rooms, and the largest is decorated with intricate wall paintings
Hasbaya.fact: The upper floor has 65 rooms, and the largest is decorated with intricate wall paintings.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: The Prince was told that between 800 and 1,000 _____ were killed here by the Druze in the fighting during 1860
Hasbaya.fact: The Prince was told that between 800 and 1,000 Christians were killed here by the Druze in the fighting during 1860.

Hasbaya.fact: A set of smaller lions appears within the arch above the doorway and just below that is a plaque in Arabic commemorating an addition to the castle made in the year 1009 Hejira by Emir Ali Chehab some 400 years ago.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: Once through the portal, you enter a huge stone paved courtyard surrounded by castle walls _____ thick
Hasbaya.fact: Once through the portal, you enter a huge stone paved courtyard surrounded by castle walls 1.5 meters thick.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: This was the entrance of the "diwan" or salon of Sitt Chams, wife of Bechir Chehab II, governor of Mount Lebanon between _____ and 1840
Hasbaya.fact: This was the entrance of the "diwan" or salon of Sitt Chams, wife of Bechir Chehab II, governor of Mount Lebanon between 1788 and 1840.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: To the left of the diwan is the wing occupied by ibrahim Pasha of Egypt during his campaign against the Ottomans in _____
Hasbaya.fact: To the left of the diwan is the wing occupied by ibrahim Pasha of Egypt during his campaign against the Ottomans in 1838.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: The strategically sited outpost was also used by the _____ emirs, who ousted the Crusaders from the area in the 1170s and rebuilt much of the citadel complex for military and residential use
Hasbaya.fact: Overlooking the modern village of Hasbaya in south Lebanon, the Chehabi Citadel occupied a strategic location for the armies of the First Crusade, who are believed to have built the original fortifications in the eleventh century. The strategically sited outpost was also used by the Chehabi emirs, who ousted the Crusaders from the area in the 1170s and rebuilt much of the citadel complex for military and residential use.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: Its main portal features a carved image of a lion, the emblem of the _____ family
Hasbaya.fact: The strategically sited outpost was also used by the Chehabi emirs, who ousted the Crusaders from the area in the 1170s and rebuilt much of the citadel complex for military and residential use. Chehabi descendants have continually occupied the site up until this day.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: There lies the ruins of an old khan where Ali, son of _____, was killed in a battle with the Ottoman army
Hasbaya.fact: There lies the ruins of an old khan where Ali, son of Fakhreddin Maan, was killed in a battle with the Ottoman army.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: In this khan, a popular weekly market held very _____ is visited by traders and visitors from all over the area
Hasbaya.fact: In this khan, a popular weekly market held very Tuesday is visited by traders and visitors from all over the area.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: Near this site flows the _____, a tributary of the Jordan River
Hasbaya.fact: Near this site flows the Hasbani, a tributary of the Jordan River.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: Hamdan was hit in the chest by a lead pellet in _____ during a demonstration near parliament, days after a deadly explosion struck Beirut's port
Hasbaya.fact: Hamdan was hit in the chest by a lead pellet in 2020 during a demonstration near parliament, days after a deadly explosion struck Beirut's port.

Hasbaya.subject: International Relations
Hasbaya.question: This was the entrance of the "diwan" or salon of Sitt Chams, wife of _____, governor of Mount Lebanon between 1788 and 1840
Hasbaya.fact: This was the entrance of the "diwan" or salon of Sitt Chams, wife of Bechir Chehab II, governor of Mount Lebanon between 1788 and 1840.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: The _____ was Syrian statesman, thrice president (1875–1960).
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Hashim al-Atassi (Arabic: هاشم الأتاسي, romanized: Hāšim al-ʾAtāsī; 11 January 1875 – 5 December 1960) was a Syrian politician and statesman who served as the President of Syria on three occasions from 1936 to 1939, 1949 to 1951 and 1954 to 1955.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He studied public administration at the Mekteb-i Mülkiye in Istanbul, and graduated in _____
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: He studied public administration at the Mekteb-i Mülkiye in Istanbul, and graduated in 1893.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He began his political career in _____ in the Ottoman vilayet of Beirut, and through the years, up to 1918, served as Governor of Homs, Hama, Baalbek, Anatolia, and Jaffa, which included the then-smal
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: He began his political career in 1888 in the Ottoman vilayet of Beirut, and through the years, up to 1918, served as Governor of Homs, Hama, Baalbek, Anatolia, and Jaffa, which included the then-small suburb of Tel Aviv.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In _____, after the defeat of Ottoman Turkey during World War I, he was elected chairman of the Syrian National Congress, the equivalent of a modern parliament
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1919, after the defeat of Ottoman Turkey during World War I, he was elected chairman of the Syrian National Congress, the equivalent of a modern parliament.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He delegated _____ to formulate alliances between Syria and Europe, in a vain attempt to prevent the implementation of a French Mandate
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: During his tenure, Atassi appointed the veteran independence activist and statesman Abd al-Rahman Shahbandar, one of the leaders of the Syrian nationalist movement against the Ottoman Empire during World War I, as Foreign Minister. He delegated Shahbandar to formulate alliances between Syria and Europe, in a vain attempt to prevent the implementation of a French Mandate.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: France moved quickly to reverse _____ independence
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: During his tenure, Atassi appointed the veteran independence activist and statesman Abd al-Rahman Shahbandar, one of the leaders of the Syrian nationalist movement against the Ottoman Empire during World War I, as Foreign Minister. France moved quickly to reverse Syrian independence.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Shahbandar's efforts to compromise with Gouraud proved futile, and Atassi's cabinet was dissolved on 24 July _____, when the French defeated the Syrian Army at the Battle of Maysalun and imposed their
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Shahbandar's efforts to compromise with Gouraud proved futile, and Atassi's cabinet was dissolved on 24 July 1920, when the French defeated the Syrian Army at the Battle of Maysalun and imposed their mandate over Syria.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: The Bloc was a political coalition movement that sought full independence for _____ through diplomatic rather than violent resistance
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: France moved quickly to reverse Syrian independence. The French High Commissioner Henri Gouraud presented Faisal with an ultimatum, demanding the surrender of Aleppo to the French Army, the dismantling of the Syrian Army, the adaptation of the French franc in Syria, and the dissolution of the Atassi government.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: It founders were a group of landowners, lawyers, civil servants, and _____-trained professionals from Damascus, Aleppo, Homs, Hama, and Lattakia
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: It founders were a group of landowners, lawyers, civil servants, and Ottoman-trained professionals from Damascus, Aleppo, Homs, Hama, and Lattakia.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Atassi was elected permanent _____ of the National Bloc
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Atassi was elected permanent President of the National Bloc. In 1928, he was also elected President of the Constituent Assembly, and charged with laying out Syria's first republican constitution.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In _____, he was also elected President of the Constituent Assembly, and charged with laying out Syria's first republican constitution
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1928, he was also elected President of the Constituent Assembly, and charged with laying out Syria's first republican constitution. In 1928 and 1932, he became a deputy for Homs in Parliament.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In _____ and 1932, he became a deputy for Homs in Parliament
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1928, he was also elected President of the Constituent Assembly, and charged with laying out Syria's first republican constitution. In 1928 and 1932, he became a deputy for Homs in Parliament.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: The assembly was dissolved by the French high commissioner in May _____ because of its adherence to the 1920 proclamation, and Atassi was imprisoned by the French for several months at Arwad Island
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: The assembly was dissolved by the French high commissioner in May 1930 because of its adherence to the 1920 proclamation, and Atassi was imprisoned by the French for several months at Arwad Island.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: After being freed, he renominated himself for the presidency but lost the first round of elections and dropped out of the second, giving his endorsement to the independent Mohammad Ali al-Abid, who be
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: After being freed, he renominated himself for the presidency but lost the first round of elections and dropped out of the second, giving his endorsement to the independent Mohammad Ali al-Abid, who became president in the summer of 1932. In 1928 and 1932, he became a deputy for Homs in Parliament.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In _____, Abid negotiated a treaty with France that promised gradual independence from the mandate but kept the Syrian Mountains under French control
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1934, Abid negotiated a treaty with France that promised gradual independence from the mandate but kept the Syrian Mountains under French control.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Atassi severely criticized the treaty, arguing that no independence was valid unless it encompassed all of _____'s territory
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1934, Abid negotiated a treaty with France that promised gradual independence from the mandate but kept the Syrian Mountains under French control. Atassi severely criticized the treaty, arguing that no independence was valid unless it encompassed all of Syria's territory.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He called for a 60-day strike to protest _____'s proposed treaty
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1934, Abid negotiated a treaty with France that promised gradual independence from the mandate but kept the Syrian Mountains under French control. He called for a 60-day strike to protest Abid's proposed treaty.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In defeat, the _____ government agreed to recognize the National Bloc leaders as the sole representatives of the Syrian people and invited Hashem al-Atassi for diplomatic talks in Paris
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In defeat, the French government agreed to recognize the National Bloc leaders as the sole representatives of the Syrian people and invited Hashem al-Atassi for diplomatic talks in Paris.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: On 22 March _____, he headed a senior Bloc delegation to France, and, over 6 months, managed to formulate a Franco-Syrian treaty of independence
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: On 22 March 1936, he headed a senior Bloc delegation to France, and, over 6 months, managed to formulate a Franco-Syrian treaty of independence. Other political, cultural, and economic attachments were made and Atassi returned to Syria in triumph on 27 September 1936.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Other political, cultural, and economic attachments were made and Atassi returned to Syria in triumph on 27 September _____
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: On 22 March 1936, he headed a senior Bloc delegation to France, and, over 6 months, managed to formulate a Franco-Syrian treaty of independence. Other political, cultural, and economic attachments were made and Atassi returned to Syria in triumph on 27 September 1936.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In return, Syria pledged to support _____ in times of war, offer the use of her air space, and the right for France to maintain military bases on Syrian territory
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: On 22 March 1936, he headed a senior Bloc delegation to France, and, over 6 months, managed to formulate a Franco-Syrian treaty of independence. In return, Syria pledged to support France in times of war, offer the use of her air space, and the right for France to maintain military bases on Syrian territory.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Hailed as a national hero, he was elected President of the Republic by a majority vote in November _____, the first head of state of the modern state of Syria
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Other political, cultural, and economic attachments were made and Atassi returned to Syria in triumph on 27 September 1936. Hailed as a national hero, he was elected President of the Republic by a majority vote in November 1936, the first head of state of the modern state of Syria.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Atassi resigned on 7 July _____ as the French continued to procrastinate about full Syrian independence and the withdrawal of French troops, and public discontent at the delay boiled over onto the str
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Atassi resigned on 7 July 1939 as the French continued to procrastinate about full Syrian independence and the withdrawal of French troops, and public discontent at the delay boiled over onto the streets.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Abd al-_____ returned to Syria at this time and agitated against Atassi and the National Block for failing to secure French ratification
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Abd al-Rahman Shahbandar returned to Syria at this time and agitated against Atassi and the National Block for failing to secure French ratification.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: The ex-_____ retired to his native Homs and spent one year in seclusion, refusing to take part in political activity
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: The ex-President retired to his native Homs and spent one year in seclusion, refusing to take part in political activity.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Following his resignation, several years of instability and _____ military rule followed
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Abd al-Rahman Shahbandar returned to Syria at this time and agitated against Atassi and the National Block for failing to secure French ratification. Atassi's resignation was also influenced by the French decision to cede the Syrian province of Alexandretta (current day Iskenderun in Hatay Province) to Turkey, enraging Syrian nationalists.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: The 1940s overall were dominated by the politics and machinations of _____ and its aftermath
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: The 1940s overall were dominated by the politics and machinations of World War II and its aftermath.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Syria was occupied by British and General Charles de Gaulle's Free French Forces, which did not leave until _____
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Syria was occupied by British and General Charles de Gaulle's Free French Forces, which did not leave until 1946.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In an attempt at appeasing the _____, de Gaulle promised independence and visited Syria to elicit support for France
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In an attempt at appeasing the Syrians, de Gaulle promised independence and visited Syria to elicit support for France.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He visited _____ al-Atassi in Homs and invited him to resume the presidency, assuring the veteran leader that France wanted to turn a new page in her relations with Syria
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: He visited Hashem al-Atassi in Homs and invited him to resume the presidency, assuring the veteran leader that France wanted to turn a new page in her relations with Syria.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Atassi refused, however, claiming that his recent experience showed that _____ could not be trusted in its promises of independence
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In an attempt at appeasing the Syrians, de Gaulle promised independence and visited Syria to elicit support for France. He visited Hashem al-Atassi in Homs and invited him to resume the presidency, assuring the veteran leader that France wanted to turn a new page in her relations with Syria.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In _____, rather than re-nominate himself, Atassi endorsed the election of Shukri al-Quwatli, a well-established Damascus leader who had risen to prominence under Atassi's patronage, as President of t
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1943, rather than re-nominate himself, Atassi endorsed the election of Shukri al-Quwatli, a well-established Damascus leader who had risen to prominence under Atassi's patronage, as President of the Republic. Atassi took no active part in the final struggle for independence but supported the Quwatli government, which lasted from 1943 to 1949.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Atassi took no active part in the final struggle for independence but supported the Quwatli government, which lasted from _____ to 1949
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1943, rather than re-nominate himself, Atassi endorsed the election of Shukri al-Quwatli, a well-established Damascus leader who had risen to prominence under Atassi's patronage, as President of the Republic. Atassi took no active part in the final struggle for independence but supported the Quwatli government, which lasted from 1943 to 1949.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Due to a tense political atmosphere, however, and increasing anti-_____ sentiment within political circles, Atassi was unable to intervene to save the administration
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1943, rather than re-nominate himself, Atassi endorsed the election of Shukri al-Quwatli, a well-established Damascus leader who had risen to prominence under Atassi's patronage, as President of the Republic. Atassi took no active part in the final struggle for independence but supported the Quwatli government, which lasted from 1943 to 1949.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In _____, while Syria was facing a prolonged cabinet crisis, President Quwatli called on his old mentor to form a government of national unity
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1947, while Syria was facing a prolonged cabinet crisis, President Quwatli called on his old mentor to form a government of national unity.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He also argued with _____ over presidential authority and conditioned that it would have to be curtailed if he became prime minister, but Quwatli refused
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In 1947, while Syria was facing a prolonged cabinet crisis, President Quwatli called on his old mentor to form a government of national unity. He also argued with President Quwatli over presidential authority and conditioned that it would have to be curtailed if he became prime minister, but Quwatli refused.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In March _____, the Quwatli government was overthrown in a coup d'état by Chief of Staff Husni al-Za'im, who headed a military cabinet for four months before he himself was overthrown in August 1949
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In March 1949, the Quwatli government was overthrown in a coup d'état by Chief of Staff Husni al-Za'im, who headed a military cabinet for four months before he himself was overthrown in August 1949.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Following this development, leading politicians called on the aging _____ to create a provisional government that would supervise national elections and the restoration of civilian rule
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Due to a tense political atmosphere, however, and increasing anti-Quwatli sentiment within political circles, Atassi was unable to intervene to save the administration. Following this development, leading politicians called on the aging Atassi to create a provisional government that would supervise national elections and the restoration of civilian rule.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He complied and formed a cabinet that included representatives of all parties, including the leftist _____ of Michel Aflaq, who he appointed Minister of Agriculture
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: He complied and formed a cabinet that included representatives of all parties, including the leftist Baath Party of Michel Aflaq, who he appointed Minister of Agriculture.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He released Munir al-_____, who was imprisoned by Husni al-Za'im, and voted him into the Constitutional Assembly
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: He released Munir al-Ajlani, who was imprisoned by Husni al-Za'im, and voted him into the Constitutional Assembly.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Under Atassi's auspices, a new electoral law was adopted, and women voted for the first time in the election of 15 and 16 November _____
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Under Atassi's auspices, a new electoral law was adopted, and women voted for the first time in the election of 15 and 16 November 1949. Atassi served as Prime Minister from August to December 1949, after which a parliamentary majority nominated him for a second term as president.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Atassi served as Prime Minister from August to December _____, after which a parliamentary majority nominated him for a second term as president
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Under Atassi's auspices, a new electoral law was adopted, and women voted for the first time in the election of 15 and 16 November 1949. Atassi served as Prime Minister from August to December 1949, after which a parliamentary majority nominated him for a second term as president.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He came into conflict with the politicians of _____ for supporting the interests of the Aleppo nobility and their desire to unite with Iraq
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: He came into conflict with the politicians of Damascus for supporting the interests of the Aleppo nobility and their desire to unite with Iraq.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He supported the _____'s Party of Aleppo and appointed its leader Nazim al-Qudsi as prime minister
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: He supported the People's Party of Aleppo and appointed its leader Nazim al-Qudsi as prime minister.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: The party was vehemently pro-Iraq and sought a union with _____
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: The party was vehemently pro-Iraq and sought a union with Baghdad.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: One of the _____ administration's most memorable actions was the closure of Syria's border with Lebanon to prevent the rampant influx of Lebanese goods into Syria
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: One of the Atassi administration's most memorable actions was the closure of Syria's border with Lebanon to prevent the rampant influx of Lebanese goods into Syria. Atassi received senior Iraqi leaders in Damascus, including Crown Prince Abd al-Illah and Faisal II of Iraq, for technical discussions on union.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: From _____ to 1951, he undertook serious talks with the Iraqi government over the union issue
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: From 1949 to 1951, he undertook serious talks with the Iraqi government over the union issue.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Atassi received senior Iraqi leaders in Damascus, including _____ al-Illah and Faisal II of Iraq, for technical discussions on union
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Atassi received senior Iraqi leaders in Damascus, including Crown Prince Abd al-Illah and Faisal II of Iraq, for technical discussions on union.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: This angered Syria's emerging military strongman _____, who claimed that the Hashemite family of Baghdad should have no jurisdiction over Damascus
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: This angered Syria's emerging military strongman Adib Shishakli, who claimed that the Hashemite family of Baghdad should have no jurisdiction over Damascus.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Shishakli demanded a change in course, yet _____ remained adamant and refused to submit to military pressure
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Atassi received senior Iraqi leaders in Damascus, including Crown Prince Abd al-Illah and Faisal II of Iraq, for technical discussions on union. Shishakli demanded a change in course, yet Atassi remained adamant and refused to submit to military pressure.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In response, _____ arrested Atassi's Chief of Staff Sami al-Hinnawi, a People's Party sympathizer, and several pro-Iraqi officers in the Syrian Army
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: This angered Syria's emerging military strongman Adib Shishakli, who claimed that the Hashemite family of Baghdad should have no jurisdiction over Damascus. Shishakli demanded a change in course, yet Atassi remained adamant and refused to submit to military pressure.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: He then demanded that one of his right-hand-men, _____, be appointed Minister of Defense, to ensure that pro-Iraqi influence in Syria remained under control
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: He then demanded that one of his right-hand-men, Colonel Fawzi Selu, be appointed Minister of Defense, to ensure that pro-Iraqi influence in Syria remained under control.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Fearing a head-on-clash with the military, _____ reluctantly accepted the demands
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: Shishakli demanded a change in course, yet Atassi remained adamant and refused to submit to military pressure. In response, Shishakli arrested Atassi's Chief of Staff Sami al-Hinnawi, a People's Party sympathizer, and several pro-Iraqi officers in the Syrian Army.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: In December _____, however, President Atassi asked Maarouf al-Dawalibi, another member of the People's Party, to form a cabinet
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: In December 1951, however, President Atassi asked Maarouf al-Dawalibi, another member of the People's Party, to form a cabinet.

Hashim al-Atassi.subject: International Relations
Hashim al-Atassi.question: Dawalibi accepted the job but refused to give the defense portfolio to _____
Hashim al-Atassi.fact: He then demanded that one of his right-hand-men, Colonel Fawzi Selu, be appointed Minister of Defense, to ensure that pro-Iraqi influence in Syria remained under control. Dawalibi accepted the job but refused to give the defense portfolio to Fawzi Selu.
